title: Introduce compact bootstrap images and atomic dependency reconciler to speed presubmit feedback
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces fast presubmit lint path and compact bootstrap images to reduce CI setup time; adds an atomic dependency reconciler to harmonize lockfiles across repo modules. No user-facing API changes.
body:
Title: Introduce compact bootstrap images and atomic dependency reconciler to speed presubmit feedback

Description: This PR reduces presubmit latency and flakiness by introducing two coordinated changes: (1) compact bootstrap images + a minimal local runner shim that cuts toolchain and network setup time for fast-presubmit lanes, and (2) an atomic dependency reconciler that can apply consistent lockfile updates across workspace modules and generate a small, auditable reconciliation plan. The changes are intentionally conservative and gated behind a new fast-presubmit lane so we can measure impact before widening.

Motivation and context: Our presubmit feedback median has increased due to expanding toolchains and noisy devcontainer bootstraps. Teams frequently open dependency PRs that drift the lockfiles for different workspace modules; that leads to duplicate CI work and merge conflicts. This work combines an engineering effort to reduce CI setup time (compact bootstrap images + minimal-runner) with an infra tool (dep-reconciler) to make dependency updates atomic and reproducible. Related: ENG-3241 (presubmit fast-lane), SUP-1123 (support ticket for lockfile drift).

What this PR changes (high-level):
- Add ci/images/compact-bootstrap.Dockerfile: a trimmed build image that contains only the runtimes and tools required for lint/typed-check quickpaths.
- Add ci/workflows/presubmit-fast.yml: a new GitHub Actions workflow for fast-presubmit lanes that uses the compact image and a minimal-runner script. This workflow runs lint, typecheck, and unit smoke tests.
- Add scripts/bootstrap-minimal.sh: shell shim to bootstrap the repo in < 20s by reusing cached toolchain layers and skipping heavy steps (no full install, no generated-bindings).
- Add tools/dep-reconciler/: small Go CLI that inspects go.mod/package.json/yarn.lock variants across modules, computes a reconciled lockfile set, and emits a single patch (with provenance) that can be applied or opened as a PR. Includes a --dry-run and --apply mode and an opt-in Linear integration.
- Update ci/helpers/cache-primer.sh to be cache-aware for the compact image and to warm workspace metadata used by the minimal runner.
- Tests and CI: unit tests for dep-reconciler, smoke tests for minimal bootstrap, integration job that validates reconciler output on a sample workspace.

Commits (summary):
- 37f3a2b: introduce compact-bootstrap image and minimal-runner shim
- 4a9e71c: add fast-presubmit workflow and cache primer updates
- 9b0c2f1: add dep-reconciler CLI, unit tests, and sample reconciliation plan

Files changed (high-level):
- ci/images/compact-bootstrap.Dockerfile
- ci/workflows/presubmit-fast.yml
- scripts/bootstrap-minimal.sh
- tools/dep-reconciler/main.go
- tools/dep-reconciler/plan_test.go
- ci/helpers/cache-primer.sh (updated)
- docs/ci/fast-presubmit.md (new)
- .github/labels/ci-annotations.md (updated)

Testing performed:
- Local: built compact image, executed bootstrap-minimal.sh on mac/linux, measured cold vs warmed startup times (cold: ~120s -> warmed: ~18s for lint path).
- Unit: dep-reconciler tests cover semver merge behavior and detection of conflicting manifests.
- CI: new presubmit-fast lane included in this PR; initial runs had one flaky external network job which was retried and passed. Full matrix kept on the standard presubmit workflows to preserve coverage.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ethan Kim (reviewer): "Nice reduction in setup time numbers. Concern: compact image might diverge from full build images and mask issues. Can we add an optional 'integration smoke' step that runs full-build in weekly scheduled job?"
- Maya (author): "Agree — added docs/ci/fast-presubmit.md to call out scope and added a weekly ci/workflows/presubmit-fast-integration.yml as a follow-up task (ENG-3287) to run full-builds on a sample subset. Kept the fast lane explicitly limited to lint/typecheck/unit-smoke for now."

- Sofia Morales: "dep-reconciler looks promising. Please add clear auditing info to the plan output (timestamp, git sha, module sources). Also ensure reconcile changes are not auto-applied without a PR in the default mode."
- Maya: "Plan output includes provenance fields and default behavior is --dry-run. --apply requires explicit flag and a service token; documented in docs/ci/dep-reconciler.md."

- Ravi Desai: "We should ensure that cache-primer changes are safe for existing runners and do not evict shared caches. Also add a small metric to track fast-presubmit success rate."
- Maya: "Adjusted cache-primer to scope cache keys to 'compact:' prefix. Added a basic CloudMetrics counter 'ci.fast_presubmit.success' increment on workflow completion; metric emitted via existing CI telemetry hook."

Author followups and fixes: 
- Reworked minimal runner to explicitly fail fast if missing critical tools rather than silently continuing.
- Reduced docker layer size by splitting the compact image into two stages and removing optional debugging packages.
- Added a small integration test that runs the reconciler against a synthetic multi-module workspace to verify patch semantics.

CI summary:
- Run 1: presubmit-fast initially failed due to external network flakiness in sample e2e fetch — retried run passed.
- Lint/test suites: pass on fast lane; full presubmit matrix unchanged and passed on this branch.
- Security scan: compact image scanned with Trivy; flagged no high-severity issues. Dep-reconciler dependencies are pinned and included in go.sum.

Rollout plan: 
- Enable fast-presubmit for core repos only for two weeks behind a feature flag. Collect telemetry (median presubmit start time, success rate, cache hit rate).
- Run ENG-3287 scheduled weekly integration job that executes full builds on a small sample to catch regressions.
- After two weeks and positive metrics, extend to more teams and add an automated bot that opens reconciler PRs on --apply requests.

Backward compatibility and risk: 
- No runtime or API compatibility changes. All changes are CI infra and tooling. The compact image intentionally omits heavy build-time artifacts so there is a risk of masking build-specific regressions; mitigations described above (weekly integration, preserved full presubmit). Dep-reconciler will not auto-apply changes unless explicitly requested.

Notes for maintainers: 
- The dep-reconciler code includes a small embedded example under tools/dep-reconciler/testdata/ that maintainers can run with 'go test ./... -run TestPlan'.
- The compact bootstrap Dockerfile includes a VERSION label; bump when base toolchain changes.

Merge outcome: Squash merged into main. Attribution: Maya Patel (author). Merge commit created and small follow-up cleanup PR opened to rename a script var (pr-197622).

If you'd like a follow-up: I can split the dep-reconciler into its own repo and add a GitHub App to open reconciliation PRs automatically (future work)."
